name: expand_code_chunks
description:
Expand line ranges or code chunks within a file and return the expanded content.

Code can be expanded by specifying line ranges or by searching for code symbols in the code, separating levels of
hierarchy with slashes.

Example patterns:
- "MyClass": Selects the class definition and any references to MyClass.
- "my_function": Selects the function definition and any uses of my_function.
- "def my_function": Selects only the function definition for my_function.
- "MyClass/my_method": Selects the method my_method within MyClass using slash separator.

file_path.title: File Path
file_path.description: The path of the file in which to select code.

patterns.title: Patterns
patterns.description:
A list of string patterns to search for and expand in the content of the file. Examples are function
names, class names, variable names, etc.

line_ranges.title: Line Ranges
line_ranges.description:
A list of tuples representing the start and end of the line ranges to expand. Note that line ranges
should use python-style indices (zero-based, non-inclusive end line). A entire file can be expanded using
[[0, -1]].

description: Find and replace code in a file.

file_path.title: File Path

find.title: Find
find.description:

characters that you want included literally.

replace.title: Replace
replace.description:
The code snippet to replace with. Use string literals when including any
special characters that you want included literally.

name: grep
description:
Search for a pattern in the content or file paths of all files in the workspace.

This function can be used in three distinct modes: content search, path search, and path-filtered content search.
1. Content Search: If only content_pattern is provided, it searches for the pattern in the content of all files.
2. Path Search: If only path_glob is provided, it searches for the pattern in the file paths.
3. Path-Filtered Content Search: If both content_pattern and path_glob are provided, it first filters the files
by the path pattern and then searches for the content pattern in the filtered files.

Example patterns:
- content_pattern = "class Myclass": Finds the class definition for Myclass in all files.
- path_glob = "*/subdir/to/*.py": Finds all Python files in the specified subdirectory.
- content_pattern = "class Myclass" and path_glob = "*/subdir/to/*.py": Finds the class definition for
Myclass in all Python files in the specified subdirectory. Note that path_glob is a glob pattern, and
content_pattern is regex.

content_pattern.title: Content Pattern
content_pattern.description:
The regex pattern to search for in the file contents. This is a regular expression, so ensure
to escape any special characters if needed.

path_glob.title: Path Glob
path_glob.description:
The glob pattern to search for in the file paths. Note that the path_glob glob should match
the full path, not just parts of it. For example, "subdir/*.py" will not match "dir/subdir/file.py", but
"*/subdir/*.py" will match it.

name: expand_folder
description: Expand a folder in the workspace.

folder_path.title: Folder Path
folder_path.description: The path of the folder to expand.

name: bash
description:
Execute a bash command on the workspace.

Commands are run in the workspace root directory. Typically used to reproduce bugs or verify features are
working as expected. Avoid making calls that will result in very large outputs, as they may be truncated. End
commands with `&` to run them in the background.

Interactive commands should be used sparingly and should be run in the background with `&` to avoid blocking.

Example commands:
- `git log --oneline -n 50`: Show the git log for the last 50 commits.
- `bash minimal_reproducible_example_script.sh`: Run a bash reproduction script in the workspace.
- `long_running_command &`: Commands ending with `&` are automatically run in background.
- `python3 -i &`: Start an interactive Python session in background.

command.title: Command
command.description:
The command to execute. Can also be an integer PID, in which case the running logs from that command
will be returned (excluding any logs that have been previously retrieved). Commands that end with `&` are
automatically run in background and their logs can be retrieved later using the PID. For interactive
processes, you can send input by using a string in the format: "PID:input", where input is what to send to
stdin.

timeout.title: Timeout
timeout.description:
Optional timeout in seconds for foreground command execution. If exceeded, the command is moved to
background and a warning with the PID is returned. Explicitly backgrounded commands using `&` do not use
this timeout for the startup window and instead use the configured startup window constant. This option is
capped at 600 seconds.

name: exit_plan_mode
description:
<summary>Exit plan mode and present your implementation plan to the user for approval.

AVAILABILITY: PLAN MODE ONLY
This tool ONLY works in PLAN mode. Check the latest <system-reminder> tag to confirm you are in plan mode.
Calling this tool in any other mode will fail with an error.

## When to Use
- Your implementation plan is ready for user approval
- The task requires code changes (not just research/exploration)

## What Happens
- User approves: You will get switched to DEFAULT mode and begin implementation
- User requests changes: You will stay in PLAN mode with feedback to address

## Before Calling
If your plan has ambiguities, use ask_user_questions first to clarify requirements.</summary>
<returns>
<description>Success message if approved, or user feedback if changes requested.</description>
</returns>

plan.description: Implementation plan in markdown format with approach, key files, and steps.

name: update_todo
description:
<summary>Create and manage a task list for tracking progress on multi-step tasks.

Use for: Complex tasks with 3+ distinct steps requiring planning and tracking.
Skip for: Single straightforward tasks, trivial operations, or conversational requests.
**MUST BE USED FOR COMPLEX TASKS ONLY**

Task lifecycle: Keep completed tasks visible as a log of work done. Only remove when no longer relevant.</summary>
<returns>
<description>Success message with todo list summary</description>
</returns>

TodoItem.description: A single todo item for task tracking.

id.description: Unique identifier for the todo item (e.g., 1, 2, 3)

content.description: Task description in imperative form, e.g., 'Fix authentication bug'

active_form.description: Task description in present continuous form, e.g., 'Fixing authentication bug'

status.description: Current status: pending (not started), in_progress (working on), or completed (finished)

TodoItem.title: TodoItem

merge.description:
If true, merge with existing todos by id (can omit unchanged fields).
If false, replace all existing todos.

name: mcp__atlassian__get_tool_schema
description:
<summary>Get the input schema for a specific tool from the atlassian toolset.

Available tools are:
<tool>get_atlassian_site_urls(): Get the current user's Atlassian site URLs</tool>
<tool>get_confluence_page(page_url, get_comments, markdown, output_file): Get the content of a Confluence page in Atlassian Document Format (ADF) JSON</tool>
<tool>get_confluence_spaces(site_url, space_key, space_name_regex, types): Get details of all available Confluence spaces or a specific Confluence space</tool>
<tool>view_confluence_descendants(page_url, max_depth, max_pages): View descendant pages of a specific page or space</tool>
<tool>view_confluence_ancestors(page_url): View all ancestors of a specific page in Confluence</tool>
<tool>get_adf_documentation(nodes, marks): Get the ADF documentation and schema for specific nodes and marks</tool>
<tool>create_confluence_page(parent_url, title, content, is_live_doc): Create a new page in Confluence in Atlassian Document Format (ADF) JSON</tool>
<tool>update_confluence_page(page_url, title, find, replace, version_message, match_index): Update an existing Confluence page</tool>
<tool>add_confluence_page_comment(page_url, comment, find, match_index): Add a comment to a Confluence page, either as a footer or inline comment</tool>
<tool>search_confluence_using_cql(site_url, cql, limit): Search content in Confluence using CQL (Confluence Query Language)</tool>
<tool>get_jira_issue(issue_url, show_transitions, show_links, get_comments, extra_fields): Get details of a Jira issue</tool>
<tool>get_jira_projects(site_url, include_issue_types, project_filter, include_custom_fields): Get visible Jira projects</tool>
<tool>create_jira_issue(project_url, issue_type, summary, description, assignee, parent_issue, fields): Create a new Jira issue in a project</tool>
<tool>update_jira_issue(issue_url, summary, description, assignee, transition, comment, fields): Update a Jira issue with various operations</tool>
<tool>search_jira_using_jql(site_url, jql, limit): Search Jira issues using JQL (Jira Query Language)</tool>
<tool>download_jira_issue_attachment(issue_url, attachment_id, workspace_path): Download an attachment from a Jira issue and return its contents</tool>
<tool>upload_jira_issue_attachment(issue_url, file_path, mime_type): Upload a file as an attachment to a Jira issue</tool></summary>
<returns>
<description>The input schema for the specified tool.</description>
</returns>

tool_name.description: The name of the tool to get the schema for.
